Both disclosures focus on the technical specifications of AMD's discrete Radeon GPUs for desktop and notebook PCs, specifically supporting DirectX 12 Ultimate and Vulkan APIs. D041 lists FreeSync and VR support, while D034 updates the architecture to RDNA 3 and mentions AI/ML computing support, but the core subject of discrete GPU API support remains consistent.

Both disclosures describe AMD's current-generation discrete desktop and notebook GPUs based on the RDNA 3 architecture (Radeon RX 7000 series). The 2023 disclosure details the architecture's features (AI/ray tracing hardware, Infinity Cache) and VRAM targets, while the 2024 disclosure confirms the continued focus on this architecture for gaming and AI/ML computing, supported by the Adrenalin software.

previous_disclosures.summary: AMD Radeon series GPUs support DirectX 12 Ultimate, Vulkan, FreeSync technologies, and VR, supported by Radeon Software tools and open-source FidelityFX toolkit for developers.

The RDNA3 architecture, powering the Radeon RX 7000 series, provides up to 96 compute units, AI/ray tracing hardware, Infinity Cache, and supports AI-accelerated video encoding and AV1 hardware encoding, targeting discrete desktop GPUs with up to 24GB VRAM and notebooks with up to 16GB.

sentences.text: Our AMD Radeon discrete GPU processors for desktop and notebook PCs support current generation application programming interfaces (APIs) like DirectX® 12 Ultimate and Vulkan®, support high-refresh rate displays and include the latest technologies for immersive gaming experiences and high-performance AI/ML computing.
Our current Radeon RX 7000 Series graphics, based on the AMD RDNA™ 3 architecture, deliver high performance for the latest gaming and creation workloads.

The Intel® Arc™ graphics family offers modern GPU features to power immersive games, creator applications, and AI workloads. In 2024, we launched the Intel Arc B-Series based on the latest Xe2 GPU architecture. The compute engine of the Intel Arc B-Series is our second-generation Xe-core, which delivers 70% more performance per core and is 50% more power efficient than the Intel Arc A750.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm disclose the use of GPUs within their broader computing architectures. AMD focuses on its discrete Radeon GPUs for desktop/notebook performance and gaming. Qualcomm describes its Adreno GPUs as part of its System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture, designed to deliver high-quality graphics performance for 3D gaming and user interfaces, enabling high-performance and low-power computing alongside CPUs and NPUs.

Our Qualcomm® Adreno™ GPUs are designed to deliver high quality graphics performance for visually rich 3D gaming and user interfaces.
